caption: The reusable framework governs a downstream project through kernel invariants, a durable control plane, the executable rail, evidence, verification, and release.
code:
flowchart TB
  Builder["Builder Program"] --> Framework["Absolute Framework"]
  Framework --> Project["Downstream Project"]
  Kernel["00 kernel invariants"] --> Control["01 control plane"]
  Control --> Runtime["10 runtime rail"]
  Runtime --> Evidence["evidence and gate"]
  Evidence --> Verify["fresh verification"]
  Verify --> Release["exact-identity release"]
  Framework --> Kernel
  Project -. feedback for future release .-> Builder
insight: Authority flows one way into a downstream project; project feedback can inform a future framework version but cannot mutate the current release.
reader_question: How does authority flow from the builder to a governed downstream release?
title: Authority and operating model

caption: Counts are derived from git ls-files; two-digit labels identify the framework's numbered domain boundaries and the machine domain model provides their full names.
insight: The distribution is documentation/data heavy, which is why a Python-only blueprint cannot stand in for the whole framework.
reader_question: Where is the release's tracked material concentrated?
title: Tracked artifacts by numbered domain

caption: For five kinds of fact this release makes, one artifact is authoritative and the rest are derived from it and checked against it.
code:
flowchart TB
  Version["VERSION — release identity"] --> Manifests["MANIFEST.json, SHA256SUMS.txt,
.absolute/release/* (derived, prepare_release_metadata.py only)"]
  Version --> RegistryCheck["FRAMEWORK.json, RELEASE_ALLOWLIST.json
(derived, checked against VERSION)"]
  Modules["Canonical module packages — module semantics"] --> ModuleIndex["MODULE_INDEX.json, AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCY_DAG.json
(derived index)"]
  Requirements["requirements.json per package — requirements and interfaces"] --> ReqRegistry["CANONICAL_REQUIREMENTS.json, INTERFACE_INDEX.json
(derived, reconciled)"]
  VerifyRun["A run of tools/deep_verify.py, bound to a tree identity — verification results"] --> TestManifest["TEST_MANIFEST.json (a description, not the surface)"]
  RootDocs["README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LIMITATIONS.md, docs/*.md — the framework's own documentation"] --> DerivedDocs["docs/ultimate-engine/ (this set — derived documentation)"]
insight: Release identity, module semantics, requirements, verification results and documentation each have exactly one authority; every other artifact is derived from it and checked against it.

title: Authority of facts
